Time has taught me that whenever this question is asked, and followed up by an anecdote about how the asker got a equivalent or better computer for cheaper, the asker is not really interested in an answer.

Some people want to pay money for the service of somebody else putting together a product that meets their needs, and putting it together well.

  • Magnetic power connectors. It will be a great day when this patent expires and every manufacturer can start doing it.
  • Aluminum unibody lends a sturdiness that is not found in plastic or multi part metal bodies
  • Ships with a *nix OS, ready for and compatible with most of the common software industry tools
  • The OS and hardware have a multibillion dollar company charged with supporting and maintaining them
  • Hardware and software are designed together, minimizing the opportunity for mismatched software updates. Not that this is not a solvable problem, but recall back in the days of Windows Vista when the weekly updates would blue screen a large swath of laptops, every week. I worked in a computer repair shop during that time - we had a list on the whiteboard of KB numbers to uninstall when a computer came in with a blue screen on Tuesday... It is easier for Apple to avoid causing such a situation due to their development practice, and as a user it is easier to choose a machine that is not susceptible to this, by choosing Apple.
  • Can also painlessly install the other two major OS flavors on it (windows & Linux)
  • The "buy one and it just works ( for most common tasks)" promise. 85% of users will require 0 setup for 85% of their use cases, and that is a powerful selling point for people (or, say, companies) interested in using a computer to complete tasks.

Upgrading their components used to be super elegant and sexy (compared to other brands of laptop at the time ) but the effort to make things small has now removed that, so I will finish with

  • Aggressive effort at small form factor is actually noticeable and convenient for me. I accept the trade.
